original_test_intent: Reset/restart the countdown of the currently configured BMC watchdog timer through the in-band path without changing its configured action or unexpectedly resetting the host.
original_method: Read the full watchdog baseline, confirm the timer's armed/action semantics and approved final state, obtain immediate authorization, issue raw 0x06 0x22 once, then verify countdown refresh and unchanged configuration/host state.
manual_activity: Operator confirms the armed watchdog action, active workload and recovery path immediately before refreshing the timer; engineer approves the intended post-countdown behavior and verdict.
safety_requirements: Do not run against an unknown or unapproved armed action.
Never use sshpass or disable host-key checking.
Do not enable, disable or reconfigure as fallback.
No host-power action or automatic retry.
Stop on unexpected reset, drift or lost management.
agent_execution_scope: Read and record complete watchdog and host baseline.
After approval issue one timer-reset request and monitor countdown/host state.
Read back final watchdog configuration and return evidence without verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve watchdog semantics, armed action and observation window.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Raw 0x06 0x22 matches Master, but unsafe transport and output-only confirmation omit the essential before/after countdown and action-state proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through verified secret-safe in-band access, issue exactly one 0x06 0x22 only after a read-only baseline confirms the approved watchdog context.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Raw bytes, Script and 10/5-minute values remain preserved; no assumed watchdog timeout is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Approved one-shot countdown refresh with baseline/readback and independent host monitor.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Project firmware with documented Reset Watchdog Timer behavior.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Pin BMC firmware, ipmitool/interface and watchdog monitor.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor watchdog command semantics and Project availability/recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds armed-action awareness and objective countdown/final-state evidence without changing raw coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: High-level `mc watchdog reset` is an override unless equivalence to raw 0x22 is approved.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Refreshing an armed watchdog can mask a pending recovery action or postpone a host reset.

project_override_considerations: A supported high-level or vendor API may perform the refresh, but raw in-band coverage remains unverified unless command equivalence and completion semantics are documented.
expected_evidence: Approval, verified target and recovery path
Complete pre-command watchdog/action/countdown and host/workload baseline
Countdown refresh plus unchanged action/configuration and host power

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Reset Watchdog Timer and raw 0x06 0x22 align. The source omits context but does not contradict the intended timer-refresh operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Once Project supplies watchdog state/action and recovery inputs, the one-shot operation is coherent; those missing inputs do not justify permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps user gating but rejects unsafe transport and incomplete evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Confirms hybrid classification and host-safety boundaries.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Restores exact raw-path accounting and objective countdown evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Separates reset/refresh from Set and Get watchdog coverage.

review_improvement: Prevents a timer refresh from running against an unknown reset action and establishes evidence that only the countdown changed.
independent_technical_reasoning: The command is standard and parameterless, so it is not inherently semantically blocked. Its safety depends on the pre-existing watchdog configuration: refreshing an armed timer can materially affect recovery timing. Immediate human confirmation is therefore intrinsic, making package/user confirmation the right classification.
